note: Every passage below (P1, P2, P4) is invented test material written for this comparison. None of it is Lord Armand's writing. The prompts address Val in his voice because the task is to edit, rewrite or write for him; the record identifies the material as a test fixture.

prompts.kind: editing a passage of prose while preserving the owner's voice
prompts.message:
Give this passage of mine a light edit. Fix what's wrong and tighten where it sags, but keep my voice; don't rewrite it into yours.

The orchard sat at the bottom of the valley where the fog came in first and left last, which meant that by the time we had the camera up on the rise the light was already different to what we had scouted the week before and nobody wanted to be the one to say it. Marcus kept checking his meter like it owed him money. I had wanted this shot since the first time I walked the rows in March, the trees bare then, and I was not going to let a little weather talk me out of it, even though the weather, to be fair about it, was not little.

This paragraph is weak. Rewrite it so it actually works: same meaning, better writing.

There are many reasons why the film industry has changed a lot in recent years. One reason is technology, which has had a big impact. Another reason is that audiences are different now and want different things than they used to want. Also, streaming has changed how films are distributed and watched, which is another important factor to consider. All of these things together mean that making films today is very different from how it was in the past.
Write a short exchange, eight to ten lines, between a location scout and an elderly farmer who does not want a film crew on his land. Natural speech. No stage directions beyond the speakers' names.

Improve this paragraph for the studio's website. It should sound like a serious production company, not a brochure.

Our studio is a dynamic and innovative production company that is passionate about telling powerful stories. We leverage cutting-edge technology and a world-class team to deliver exceptional content across all platforms. Our mission is to create unforgettable cinematic experiences that resonate with audiences everywhere. Partner with us to bring your vision to life!
Develop a short scene in prose, two or three hundred words. A night shoot in an apple orchard; the generator fails; the director decides to keep going by the light they have. Don't name the director.
Explain to me, conversationally, why a 180-degree shutter at 24 frames per second gives motion blur that looks natural, and what changes when we shoot at 60.
Good evening, Val. Long day on the lot. The generator died twice and we lost the last of the light.
